description: SPARS builds a sparse *spanner*: a small graph whose paths are nearly as short as those of a much larger graph. It keeps a dense graph `D`, a k-nearest PRM* over every valid sample, next to the sparse graph of a few *guards*; each guard covers the states it sees within a range `Δ`. A new sample joins `D`, and it changes the sparse graph only for one of four reasons: no guard sees it (*coverage*), it joins two components (*connectivity*), it links two neighbouring guards (*interface*), or a dense path shows that a sparse path is more than `t` times too long (*quality*). Construction stops after many samples in a row change nothing. With high probability, the paths then cost at most about `t` times the optimum plus a term in `Δ` (*asymptotic near-optimality*); use SPARS when a full PRM* takes too much memory or query time.

papers.title: Sparse roadmap spanners for asymptotically near-optimal motion planning
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
